The honest answer has almost nothing to do with benchmark screenshots and everything to do with how many requests land on your endpoint at the same second, and what hardware you actually own. Below is the decision path I use, followed by the commands that get either engine behind an OpenAI-compatible /v1 API. Budget around 45 minutes for one engine end-to-end, or roughly 75 if you want to run both and compare. It's intermediate territory — you should be comfortable with a terminal, cmake , and a Python virtualenv. What actually separates the two engines llama.cpp is a C/C++ inference engine that runs GGUF files.

articles.title: What Is Involuntary Churn? (Failed Payments, Not Cancellations)
articles.excerpt: Originally published on the RetryFix blog. A churn dashboard counts every ended subscription the same way: one more customer gone. Some of those customers decided to leave. Others never decided anythi…
articles.body: Originally published on the RetryFix blog . A churn dashboard counts every ended subscription the same way: one more customer gone. Some of those customers decided to leave. Others never decided anything. A renewal charge failed, the retries ran out, and the subscription lapsed. The dashboard files both under churn, and they are not the same problem. Involuntary churn is a subscription that ends because a payment failed, not because the customer cancelled. Nobody clicked cancel. The card expired, the bank declined the renewal, or the account was short on the day, and the subscription ended before anyone fixed it. This page defines the term, sets it against voluntary churn, covers why failed payments cause it, and lists what recovers the revenue.

articles.body: Launch Chrome, attach to CDP, and extract structured data with a zero-dependency Python service Most Python browser automation tutorials begin with pip install playwright and end with page.click() . That is a good default. Playwright is mature, it handles waits, and it lets you forget that a browser is a separate operating-system process. But sometimes you need to see the layer underneath. Maybe you are debugging a scraper that hangs once every thousand pages. Maybe you need the JSON response behind an infinite scroll, not the DOM that happens to be rendered. Maybe you want to attach to a Chrome instance that is already running with a logged-in profile. Or maybe you just want to stop treating one of the most complicated programs on your machine as a black box.

articles.title: How can next-token prediction learn math? Start with one trainable parameter
articles.excerpt: Next-token prediction is an objective, not a restriction that a model must only count neighboring words. A tiny model makes one part of the distinction visible. We supply the structure y_hat = w*x and…
articles.body: Next-token prediction is an objective, not a restriction that a model must only count neighboring words. A tiny model makes one part of the distinction visible. A model we can fully inspect We supply the structure y_hat = w*x and train only w . Examples use x=3 with target 6 and x=5 with target 10. The model does not discover multiplication: multiplication is built in. With squared loss (w*x-y)^2 , the gradient is 2*x*(w*x-y) . For this demonstration, a learning rate of 1/(4*x*x) halves the distance from w to 2 at every step. Starting from w=1, the first updates produce 1.5 and 1.75. After 10 updates, w=1.9990234375. Try an unseen input For x=7, without further updates, the output is 13.9931640625, approximately 14.

articles.title: AG-UI Protocol: How Event-Based Streaming Replaces Request/Response for Agent-to-Frontend Communication
articles.excerpt: Agents stream tokens, pause for tool calls, spawn subagents, and wait for human input. Traditional request/response patterns break under this workload. Every agent framework (LangChain, CrewAI, Mastra…
articles.body: Agents stream tokens, pause for tool calls, spawn subagents, and wait for human input. Traditional request/response patterns break under this workload. Every agent framework (LangChain, CrewAI, Mastra, Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, Pydantic AI) implements its own streaming format, and every frontend team writes custom adapters to consume it. AG-UI is a bidirectional event protocol that standardizes agent-to-client communication. The agent emits typed events (token deltas, tool invocations, state transitions, human-in-the-loop pauses), and any client (web, mobile, terminal, Slack) can render them without knowing which framework produced the agent. The same agent can power multiple surfaces without rewiring. The protocol has 19,683 GitHub stars and is trending #1 for TypeScript.

articles.title: A Core Merge Is Not a Feature
articles.excerpt: The work isn’t done when the PR merges. It’s done when someone can use it. A word from our VP of Engineering Emilie Schario Nobody uses Kilo Core directly. They use VS Code, JetBrains, the CLI, Agent…
articles.body: The work isn’t done when the PR merges. It’s done when someone can use it. A word from our VP of Engineering Emilie Schario Nobody uses Kilo Core directly. They use VS Code, JetBrains, the CLI, Agent Manager, or Desktop. Core is the shared code that powers all of those experiences. This distinction matters because merging code is not the same thing as shipping value to a customer. At Kilo, we've always optimized for getting value into users' hands as quickly as possible. We don't organize our work around monthly releases, big launches, or waiting until every client has the same functionality. We organize around one question: What's the smallest thing we can ship that delivers value to a user? And then we ship it.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.body: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch
articles.excerpt: See the most epic photos from SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight and historic launch tower catch.
articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.
articles.author: Josh Dinner
